chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Mae West asks Danny to play an effeminate walk-on
summary: Mae West asked Danny to do a comic effeminate bit in the prizefight scene as a punchline.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So Rudy Toones, he said, "Man, you got it made, boy." Mae West done went for you like a ton of bricks." So I waited and I went to her dressing room after, when she got through. So Miss Burgorne(?) said, "Miss West is ready to speak to you." So I went in the room. She said, "I've never noticed you on the show before." I said, "Well, I've been here, Miss West." She said, "Yeah. Well, I've got an extra part for you in the show. I wish you would consider it." I said, "Doing what?" She said, "Have you ever done any acting?" I said, "No." She said, "It's very simple." I want a punch line for my show. I want to get a wonderful laugh."

She said, "You know the scene where everybody..." It's a prize-fighting scene. It's in the front of an arena, the opening gate, where people pay to go to the ticket box and go in. And it's happy. Everybody is going to the
championship fight. She makes her entrance, and she goes in there with Money Johnson on her arm.

So this scene, how they did that, everybody rotated. They'd go on stage, run back, put on another hat, kept coming around, and it looked like a whole lot of people going in, see. So she said, "For the last scene, I want you... When you come on, you do this." Just like a...

DANNY BARKER: Yeah, like a fairy. "See, when you go in there and close that scene, that will be a terrific laugh." I said, "Well, I don't know about doing that." "You see, I'll show you. Hold your hand like this. Now, snap your fingers, see." [SNAPS] I said, "I'll think about it." She said, "Think about it."
